candidate.title: Safe-SeqS
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina overview of Safe-SeqS (Safe-Seq; Safe-Sequencing System), specifically the depicted route that uses randomly sheared DNA ends as molecular identifiers, followed by adapter ligation, the combined amplification/solid phase capture block, sequencing and family-aware interpretation. This is one linear schematic with no alternative target workflow. The left rare-mutation inset explains the aim. PCR-introduced UID adaptations, SiMSen-Seq, NOIR sequencing and product names elsewhere in the catalogue are outside this extraction. The source depicts a broad library-preparation architecture rather than an executable protocol.

An orange mark indicates the pre-existing variant in the explanatory inset and the main DNA drawing.
The left inset is descriptive context, not a separate processed branch. No end-group chemistry or strand polarity is specified.

operations.label: Shear
operations.description: Fragment the input DNA at variable boundaries, producing shorter DNA molecules whose randomly sheared ends serve as the depicted molecular identifiers; the mutation remains in its containing fragment.
operations.mechanism: DNA shearing; the source specifies no particular physical instrument or enzymatic mechanism.
operations.information_effect: Creates an end-based association between each fragment and its subsequent copies while retaining the fragment insert sequence.
